name: Mr. Heater Portable Buddy (MH9BX)
amazonQuery: Mr. Heater Portable Buddy MH9BX propane heater
summary: The go-to indoor-safe propane heater for outages: 4,000 or 9,000 BTU, rated for up to 225 sq ft, with an oxygen depletion sensor and a tip-over shutoff.
verdict:
The Mr. Heater Portable Buddy, model MH9BX, is the emergency heater most households should own: it warms one closed-off room, needs no electricity, and carries the safety devices that matter indoors.

**Two settings, one room.** Mr. Heater rates it at 4,000 or 9,000 BTU per hour for spaces up to 225 square feet, about the size of a large bedroom. It lights with a piezo igniter and burns a 1-lb propane cylinder, or a 20-lb tank through an optional hose and filter.

**Do the fuel math.** Mr. Heater lists about 3 hours on high and 6 hours on low per 1-lb cylinder, and some retailers quote closer to 2.4 and 5.4 hours. A 12-hour winter night on low takes two cylinders, so six cylinders cover about three nights. For longer outages, the hose and filter let a 20-lb tank, which holds about 20 times the propane, run it for roughly 100 hours on low.

**Safety is why it is on this list.** An oxygen depletion sensor shuts the burner off if oxygen in the room falls, and a tip-over switch kills the flame if it is knocked over. Mr. Heater rates it for indoor use up to 7,000 feet. You still need to open a window or door to the size the manual specifies, keep the stated clearance from bedding and curtains, and run a battery [CO alarm](/gear/first-alert-co400/) in the same room.

Owners report it is simple and dependable; the main complaints are short runtime on 1-lb cylinders and a front grille hot enough to scorch fabric. For a living room, step up to the [Big Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-big-buddy/). It leads our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

faqs.a: Mr. Heater rates it as indoor-safe because it has an oxygen depletion sensor and a tip-over shutoff, but safe use depends on you. name: Mr. Heater Big Buddy (MH18B)
amazonQuery: Mr. Heater Big Buddy MH18B propane heater
summary: The larger Buddy: three settings up to 18,000 BTU for rooms up to 450 sq ft, two 1-lb cylinders onboard, and the same ODS and tip-over safety shutoffs.
verdict:
The Mr. Heater Big Buddy, model MH18B, is the heater to buy when your warm room is a living room or the whole family is bunking together in one space.

**More heat for more room.** Mr. Heater lists three settings, 4,000, 9,000 and 18,000 BTU per hour, and rates it for spaces up to 450 square feet, double the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/). It holds two 1-lb propane cylinders onboard and connects to a 20-lb tank with an optional hose. Many versions include a fan that runs on D batteries to push heat across a larger room, but some current units ship without the fan, so check the listing.

**High is for warming up, not for all night.** Listings based on the manual give roughly 3 hours on high and 12 hours on low from two 1-lb cylinders, and the manual lists 50 to 220 hours on two 20-lb cylinders. Bring a cold room up on high, then drop to low or medium and let it hold. The manual calls for a larger fresh-air opening at higher output and notes that runtime falls below 20°F, where a 20-lb tank works better.

**Same safety core.** It has the oxygen depletion sensor and tip-over shutoff of the smaller Buddy heaters, plus piezo ignition. Run a battery [CO alarm](/gear/first-alert-co400/) in the room, keep clearances from bedding, and never leave it unattended.

Owners report it heats a large room quickly; the main complaints are its size and fuel use on high. If you heat only one bedroom, the Portable Buddy is easier to keep fueled. See the [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

faqs.q: How long will the Big Buddy run on a 20-lb tank?
faqs.a: The MH18B manual lists 50 to 220 hours on two 20-lb cylinders, so a single 20-lb tank gives roughly 25 to 110 hours depending on the setting. On high (18,000 BTU) expect the short end; on low (4,000 BTU) the long end. Very cold weather, below about 20°F, reduces runtime.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Big Buddy and the Portable Buddy?
faqs.a: The Big Buddy adds an 18,000 BTU setting, heats up to 450 square feet instead of 225, holds two 1-lb cylinders instead of one, and many versions add a fan. The Portable Buddy is smaller, lighter and cheaper to keep fueled, which makes it the better choice for a single bedroom.

name: Mr. Heater Little Buddy (MH4B)
amazonQuery: Mr. Heater Little Buddy MH4B propane heater
summary: Mr. Heater's smallest indoor-safe heater: 3,800 BTU for up to 95 sq ft and about 5.6 hours per 1-lb cylinder; ideal for a bathroom, small bedroom or as a second unit.
verdict:
The Mr. Heater Little Buddy, model MH4B, is a sensible small-room heater and a good backup unit, but its output is too low to be the only heat in most homes.

**Small and frugal.** Mr. Heater lists a single 3,800 BTU per hour setting for spaces up to 95 square feet, with a run time of about 5.6 hours per 1-lb cylinder. The cylinder threads into the base, so the whole unit is about the size of a coffee can on a stand, and it lights with a one-button piezo igniter.

**Size it to the room.** 95 square feet is roughly a 9-by-10-foot room: a small bedroom, a bathroom or a tent. Two cylinders cover most of a long winter night, and six cylinders last about three nights. With no high setting, it cannot recover a room that has already dropped into the 40s, so start it early and keep doors closed. For a bigger room, the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/) more than doubles the output.

**Same safety devices.** It has an oxygen depletion sensor and a tip-over shutoff, and Mr. Heater rates it for indoor use up to 7,000 feet. Because the cylinder sits underneath, it stands tall and needs a stable, level surface away from feet and pets. Open a window as the manual directs and run a battery [CO alarm](/gear/first-alert-co400/) nearby.

Owners report it is handy for bathrooms and ice-fishing shelters; the main complaint is the single heat level. It appears in the [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup and pairs well with a [heated throw](/gear/sunbeam-heated-throw/).

name: First Alert CO400 CO Alarm
amazonQuery: First Alert CO400 battery carbon monoxide alarm
summary: A battery-powered CO alarm with an electrochemical sensor and 85 dB siren; buy it before any heater, because it keeps working when the grid is down.
verdict:
The First Alert CO400 is the first thing to buy for winter outage heating: a battery-powered carbon monoxide alarm that keeps working when the power is out.

**Why battery power matters.** Hardwired CO alarms without battery backup go silent when the grid drops, which is exactly when people start running propane heaters and generators. The CO400 runs on a 9V battery, and First Alert lists an electrochemical sensor, an 85-decibel alarm, an end-of-life warning and a 7-year limited warranty. Like other UL 2034 alarms, it sounds when CO builds to a dangerous level over time.

**Place it where the risk is.** Put one in the room where a heater runs, one in or near each sleeping area, and one on every level of the house. A propane heater like the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/) is rated indoor-safe only when ventilation and placement are right; the alarm is your check that they are. Never run a [generator](/best-gas-generator/) in a garage or near open windows, whatever an alarm says. Test it monthly and before any storm you can see coming.

**Know its limits.** It has no digital display, so it will not show low but rising levels before the alarm threshold. Some models from First Alert and Kidde add a readout, which is worth having if you heat with fuel often. Replace the battery on schedule and the whole alarm when its end-of-life warning sounds.

Owners report it is cheap, loud and easy to place; the main complaint is the lack of a display. It is the must-have first purchase in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) guide.

faqs.q: Where should I put a CO alarm when using a propane heater?
faqs.a: Put one in the same room as the heater, at the height the alarm's manual recommends, and out of the heater's direct airflow. Add one in or near every sleeping area and on each level of the house. If a generator runs outside, place one near the doors and windows closest to it as well.

name: Sunbeam Microplush Heated Throw
amazonQuery: Sunbeam microplush heated throw blanket 50 x 60
summary: A 50-by-60-inch electric heated throw with three heat settings and auto shutoff; on a power station it keeps one person warm for hours on very little energy.
verdict:
A Sunbeam Microplush heated throw is the smartest way to turn stored battery power into warmth: it heats the person, not the room.

**Tiny draw, big effect.** Sunbeam's 50-by-60-inch throws have three heat settings on most versions and a 3-hour auto shutoff. One retailer lists this model at 115 watts, and lower settings use less. Check the label on yours. Compare that with a 1,500-watt space heater like the [Lasko 754200](/gear/lasko-754200-ceramic-heater/), which drains a 1,000Wh station in about 35 minutes.

**Power station math.** At an average of 60 watts, a 1,000Wh station such as the [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/) runs the throw for roughly 14 hours once inverter losses are counted, a full night with charge to spare. A 500Wh unit still covers about 7 hours. Use the [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) with your throw's rated watts, and put a sleeping bag or comforter on top to hold the heat in.

**The auto shutoff is a trade-off.** The 3-hour timer is a safety feature, but it means someone may wake up to restart it. Use it on top of you, not folded or tucked under a mattress, and follow Sunbeam's instructions. It does nothing for pipes or room temperature, so pair it with a propane heater like the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/) if the house is getting dangerously cold.

Owners report it is soft and warms up fast; the main complaint is resetting the timer. It is the electric option in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

faqs.q: Does the Sunbeam heated throw turn off by itself?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Sunbeam Microplush throws have a 3-hour auto shutoff, and some newer versions use a 4-hour timer with four heat settings. The shutoff is a safety feature, but during an outage it means you may need to press the controller again in the night to keep the throw warm.

name: Coleman North Rim 0°F Sleeping Bag
amazonQuery: Coleman North Rim 0 degree mummy sleeping bag
summary: A synthetic 0°F mummy bag that turns body heat into warmth with no fuel, power or ventilation; the cheapest, safest way to sleep through a cold-house outage.
verdict:
The Coleman North Rim is the most underrated piece of winter outage gear: a 0°F mummy bag that burns nothing, draws nothing and keeps you warm with your own body heat.

**The rating gives you margin.** Coleman rates it for 0°F and fills it with Coletherm hollow polyester insulation. Read that number as a survival limit, not a comfort promise; most people sleep comfortably well above a bag's lower rating. Indoors, where a cold house might drift into the 40s, that margin is exactly what you want. The mummy hood holds heat around your head and shoulders, where you lose the most.

**Fits most adults.** The standard bag fits sleepers up to about 6 feet 2 inches, and Coleman also sells a Big & Tall version. It is heavy and bulky next to a backpacking bag, but weight does not matter on a bedroom floor.

**Make it work harder.** Put a foam pad or mattress underneath, because the floor pulls heat away faster than air does. A family sleeping in cold-rated bags in one closed-off room can get through a night with no heater at all, which lets a small propane heater like the [Little Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-little-buddy/) simply take the edge off in the evening. If the mummy shape feels confining, unzip it and use it as a quilt over a [heated throw](/gear/sunbeam-heated-throw/).

Owners report it is warm for the price; the main complaints are bulk and a snug fit for broad shoulders. It is the zero-energy pick in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

faqs.q: Is the Coleman North Rim warm enough for a house with no heat?
faqs.a: For nearly every outage, yes. It is rated for 0°F, and an unheated house rarely falls below the 30s or 40s indoors. Put a pad or mattress underneath, wear a hat and dry layers, and close off one room so the family shares body heat. Read 0°F as a survival limit, not a comfort rating.

faqs.a: They do different jobs. A sleeping bag keeps you warm with no fuel, fumes or fire risk, but it does nothing for the room or your pipes. A propane heater like the Portable Buddy warms the air but needs ventilation, fuel and a CO alarm. Most households do best with bags for sleeping and a heater for evenings.

name: Lasko 754200 Ceramic Heater
summary: A small 1,500-watt ceramic heater with a 900-watt low setting and adjustable thermostat; useful on a generator or large battery, wasteful on a portable power station.
verdict:
The Lasko 754200 is a good small electric heater and a poor partner for most battery backup, so buy it only if you have a generator or a large home battery.

**The numbers.** Lasko's spec sheet lists 1,500 watts on high (12.7 amps, about 5,118 BTU per hour) and 900 watts on low (about 3,070 BTU), plus a fan-only mode and an adjustable thermostat. It has automatic overheat protection and a cool-touch exterior. It does not have a tip-over switch, so set it on a flat, open floor away from foot traffic.

**Why batteries struggle.** A 1,000Wh power station delivers roughly 850 usable watt-hours after inverter losses, which runs this heater about 35 minutes on high or just under an hour on low. Even a 3,600Wh station lasts only about two hours on high. A [heated throw](/gear/sunbeam-heated-throw/) at around 60 watts runs most of a night on the same 1,000Wh.

**Where it makes sense.** On a portable generator running outside, 1,500 watts is an easy load; check your total in the [generator wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/) first. Whole-home batteries and big stations recharged by solar or a generator also handle it. Electric resistance heat produces no combustion gases, a real advantage over propane in a closed room. Plug it straight into a wall outlet or a heavy cord rated for the load, keep 3 feet of clearance, and never leave it running unattended.

Owners report it heats a small room quickly and quietly; the main complaint is the missing tip-over switch. It is the generator-owner pick in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

name: Mr. Heater Hunting Buddy (MH12HB)
amazonQuery: Mr. Heater Hunting Buddy MH12HB propane heater
summary: A 6,000/12,000 BTU indoor-safe Buddy heater rated for up to 300 sq ft, sized between the Portable and Big Buddy; built for blinds, cabins and mid-size rooms.
verdict:
The Mr. Heater Hunting Buddy, model MH12HB, sits between the Portable Buddy and the Big Buddy, and it is the right size for a mid-size room, a cabin or a deer blind.

**The in-between output.** Mr. Heater lists two settings, 6,000 and 12,000 BTU per hour, for spaces up to 300 square feet. That covers a 15-by-20-foot room, where the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/) at 225 square feet falls short and the [Big Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-big-buddy/) is more than you need. It runs on one 1-lb propane cylinder, or a 20-lb tank with an optional hose.

**Fuel goes quickly.** Retailer and owner answers put runtime at about 1.8 hours on high and 3.5 hours on low per 1-lb cylinder, so a winter night on low takes three or four cylinders. For anything longer than an evening, a hose and a 20-lb tank make far more sense; owners report about 72 hours on low from one tank. Warm the room on high, then drop to low.

**Safety and build.** It carries the oxygen depletion sensor and tip-over shutoff that make the Buddy line indoor-rated, and Mr. Heater lists a 7,000-foot elevation limit. At about 16 pounds, it is heavier than the Portable Buddy, with a camo finish aimed at hunters. Ventilate as the manual directs and keep a battery [CO alarm](/gear/first-alert-co400/) in the room.

Owners report it heats blinds and ice shanties fast; the main complaints are short runtime on 1-lb cylinders and a 1-year warranty versus 3 years on the Portable Buddy. Compare it with the picks in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

name: Mr. Heater Buddy FLEX
amazonQuery: Mr. Heater Buddy FLEX 11,000 BTU propane heater
summary: An indoor-safe propane heater rated up to 11,000 BTU and about 275 sq ft, with electronic ignition and a 9,000-foot elevation limit; part of Mr. Heater's FLEX system.
verdict:
The Mr. Heater Buddy FLEX is the modern take on the Buddy heater, worth a look if you want a little more output than the Portable Buddy or you live at elevation.

**Output, coverage and altitude.** Mr. Heater rates the FLEX at up to 11,000 BTU per hour for spaces up to about 275 square feet, between the [Portable Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-portable-buddy/) at 225 and the [Hunting Buddy](/gear/mr-heater-hunting-buddy/) at 300. Retailers list the low setting at either 6,000 or 8,000 BTU, so check the version you buy. It lights with electronic ignition and weighs about 11 pounds. It is rated to 9,000 feet, versus 7,000 for the classic Buddy heaters, and since oxygen depletion sensors are sensitive to thin air, that extra 2,000 feet matters in the mountain West.

**Fuel use.** Retailers list about 2 hours on high and 3.5 hours on low per 1-lb cylinder, a burn of roughly 0.12 gallons per hour on high. A long night on low takes three or four cylinders, so plan on a 20-lb tank and hose for multi-day outages. Mr. Heater also sells FLEX accessories, including a cooking attachment, which makes it more useful at camp.

**Buy the indoor version.** Mr. Heater sells an indoor-approved FLEX and a separate outdoor-only model; only the indoor one belongs in an outage plan. Keep a battery [CO alarm](/gear/first-alert-co400/) in the room and ventilate as the manual directs.

Owners report easy lighting and a compact shape; the main complaint is short runtime on 1-lb cylinders. See the full field in our [best indoor heater for a power outage](/best-indoor-heater-for-power-outage/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Buddy FLEX and the Portable Buddy?
faqs.a: The FLEX is rated up to 11,000 BTU and about 275 square feet versus 9,000 BTU and 225 square feet for the Portable Buddy. It uses electronic ignition instead of piezo and is rated to 9,000 feet instead of 7,000. The Portable Buddy runs longer per 1-lb cylinder, about 6 hours on low versus 3.5.

faqs.q: Is the Mr. Heater Buddy FLEX safe indoors?
faqs.a: The indoor-approved version is, used as the manual directs. Mr. Heater also sells an outdoor-only FLEX, so confirm the model before you buy. Indoors, open a window or door to the size the manual requires, keep clearances from bedding and curtains, and run a battery CO alarm in the same room.
